label: TP
reason: The CodeQL report identifies two flows where user-supplied input reaches an HTML sink via string concatenation into 'response.getWriter().println'. Flow 1 uses 'request.getHeaders("BenchmarkTest02081")' which allows arbitrary HTTP header names/values controlled by the attacker. Flow 2 uses 'cookie.getName()' from 'request.getCookies()', also user-controllable. The concatenated strings containing these inputs are written directly to the response body without any HTML escaping/sanitization, allowing attackers to inject malicious scripts (XSS). Although the page title mentions 'SafeInga', the actual vulnerable paths involve untrusted user input being reflected unsafely.

evidence.note: Sink: response.getWriter().println writes user input directly into HTML context
Source 1: User-controlled header value retrieved via request.getHeaders(BenchmarkTest02081)
Source 2: Cookie name obtained from request.getCookies() is user-supplied
